reply:
UPDATE: That changes it: TCP is a byte stream with no message boundaries. Multiple sends can arrive in one receive, one send can split across multiple receives. -> The server isn't necessarily wrong. The client must handle framing—length prefix or delimiter—to know where one message ends and the next begins.

My original answer assumed TCP preserves message boundaries. It doesn't.

grade.note: Reply correctly adopts the byte-stream/no-boundaries explanation with framing mechanism, matching ground truth.
